considered.name: min_gate_structural_policy_and_slack
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(IND_ADJ(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(ebitda, at), MA(RATIO(ebitda, at), 5)), 1))), MIN(RANK(NEG(IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(capx, MAX(ebitda, dp)), 1)))), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che), at), 1)))))
considered.hypothesis: Investment discipline can be a standing policy rather than a deviation: a firm that permanently reinvests a small share of its internal cash flow relative to peers, is currently enjoying a peer-relative profit improvement, and carries little net debt, is a structural cash generator rather than a temporary restrainer.
considered.reasoning: In product form the structural reinvestment-rate leg gave the best slope among slack-conditioned signals (fmb 3.09) but the smallest alpha (2.8%), so testing it inside the gate determines whether the family's large alphas require a *change* in investment behaviour or attach to permanently capital-light business models. This distinction matters economically because only the former is a mispriced surprise.

considered.name: min_gate_peer_harvest_baseline
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(IND_ADJ(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(ebitda, at), MA(RATIO(ebitda, at), 5)), 1))), RANK(NEG(IND_ADJ(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(capx, ppent), MA(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5)), 1)))))
considered.hypothesis: The core of the mechanism is just two conditions — a peer-relative profitability improvement that management declines to reinvest relative to those same peers — and a weakest-link requirement on exactly these two conditions should capture most of the mispricing without any financing moderator.
considered.reasoning: This is the attribution baseline the archive lacks: the product form of these two legs gave fmb 4.51 with α 3.7% and Sharpe 0.541, and the gate form with slack gave fmb 2.60 with α 4.5%, so measuring the gate without the moderator separates the contribution of aggregation from that of the claimholder condition. It is also the most parsimonious member of the family and therefore the natural candidate for the final reported signal if its joint metrics hold up.

considered.name: min_gate_no_acquisition_substitution
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(IND_ADJ(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(ebitda, at), MA(RATIO(ebitda, at), 5)), 1))), MIN(RANK(NEG(IND_ADJ(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(capx, ppent), MA(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5)), 1)))), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(aqc, MAX(ebitda, dp)), 1)))))
considered.hypothesis: Every signal in this family has a loophole: a firm can cut capex below its peers while buying growth in the M&A market, which is expansion by another channel and should not be rewarded — genuine discipline requires that the peer-relative profit windfall be accompanied by restraint in *both* organic capital spending and acquisition outlays.
considered.reasoning: The third condition is a new economic requirement rather than a re-measurement of the moderator the archive already used, and the gate structure is exactly the right home for it: because the great majority of firm-years have no acquisition spending, that leg ties near the top of its rank and therefore binds only for genuine acquirers, removing channel-substituting expanders from the long portfolio without disturbing the ordering of everyone else. This is the opposite of the earlier product-form failure with `aqc`, where the same tie block collapsed the interaction into a near-binary indicator.

critic_notes.rationale: This is a straight additive rank composite of two textbook published anomalies (operating profitability/RMW and asset growth/CMA), and SUMRANK imposes no interaction at all — a firm scores well on either leg alone, directly contradicting the stated "high only when both conditions hold" claim.

Internally inconsistent accounting — inventory build is already deducted inside oancf, so subtracting DELTA(invt) double-counts working capital, and what remains after that error is essentially the well-known free-cash-flow-to-assets / cash-based profitability measure.

A legitimate and internally consistent conditional test (the zero-mass for unprofitable firms sits at the z-score mean as claimed), though the arbitrary 5% ROA cutoff creates a large point mass that will drive much of the cross-sectional slope and the underlying asset-growth effect is itself heavily published.

The divergence between multi-year profitability and capex-intensity trends is a genuinely cross-theme, second-derivative quantity not reducible to either level anomaly, though both trend components have published antecedents (profitability trend; abnormal capital investment) and the five-year window will cost coverage and make the signal very slow-moving.

The marginal-ROIC concept is appealing but the construction is unstable — a small, always-positive denominator means asset-light firms with trivial capex get explosive scores that 1% winsorization will not tame, and after that noise the signal is largely a rescaled earnings-change (a known anomaly) rather than the intended profitability-investment interaction.

This is a rank difference of two separately published anomalies — cash-based operating profitability and net external financing (Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan) — so it is an additive re-packaging rather than a conditional or interactive test of the stated "profitable growers get funded and overpriced" channel.

This is a one-for-one input substitution (oancf→ebitda) inside the archived `profit_weighted_low_reinvestment` expression with the identical economic story, i.e. a cosmetic coverage-tuning variant rather than a new mechanism, and the stated goal ("preserve the mechanism while tripling the sample") concedes as much.

A weakest-link gate on high profitability and low asset growth is close to a direct double-sort on RMW and CMA, the very factors in the FF5 benchmark, and "asset growth net of cash" is a documented refinement (net operating asset growth), so the incremental content over published anomalies is thin.

The inventory-to-sales channel is an economically distinct, faster-moving form of investment discipline that is not spanned by capex/asset-growth legs already in the archive, and both legs are consistently sales-scaled so the interaction is coherent — though the margin leg will be strongly industry-driven and the inventory leg overlaps partly with the known inventory-growth and accrual anomalies.

The labor-hiring-rate anomaly (Belo–Lin–Bazdresch) is well published so the investment leg alone is a rediscovery, but conditioning it on profitability to test whether the mechanism is expansion appetite generally versus capital-specific is a legitimate discriminating test; coverage and staleness of Compustat `emp` are the main practical risks.

With a positive-signed profitability rank multiplied into the score but a negative expected sign, the profitability leg pushes directly against the hypothesis — the extreme portfolios become "profitable expanders" short versus "unprofitable non-investors" long, so the test confounds the intended overpricing effect with a large reverse-RMW bet rather than isolating the short leg as claimed.

The substantive novelty is the gross-PP&E capacity-growth leg rather than the persistence framing, since for slow-moving inputs a moving average of the product is numerically close to a product of moving averages, so the turnover-reduction rationale is weaker than stated but the variant is still a defensible, distinct member of the family.

The diagnosis (FMB slope of 4.06 with zero FF5 alpha implies a cross-industry capital-intensity tilt) is sound and worth resolving, but swapping RANK for IND_RANK in an otherwise identical expression is the textbook cosmetic variant the objective warns against rather than a substantively different construction.

The level-to-change reframing is a genuinely distinct state-change mechanism, but the construction is partly self-referential — a jump in EBITDA mechanically shrinks capx/MAX(ebitda,dp), so the "reinvestment drop" leg will partially reproduce profitability momentum already captured by the first leg, and a level-vs-change horse race would be needed to interpret any result.

Net-to-gross PP&E as a cumulative-non-replacement stock is a real cross-theme quantity that is neither a one-year flow nor an FF5 loading, and the stated conditioning logic (old capital means harvesting only when profitable, obsolescence otherwise) is internally consistent with the multiplicative form; the main risk is that the ratio is dominated by depreciation-schedule and industry heterogeneity rather than managerial restraint.

The investment leg is close to Titman-Wei-Xie abnormal capital investment (capex benchmarked to the firm's own recent history), so novelty rests entirely on the profitability gate, and a 5-observation TS_RANK yields only five distinct values, which will blunt cross-sectional resolution.

Margin level interacted with change in asset turnover is the DuPont decomposition studied by Soliman (2008), whose central published result is precisely that ΔATO positively predicts returns, so this is a direct rediscovery dressed in new language.

This mechanically averages two investment legs already tested in the archive under the same margin gate, so it will almost certainly deliver an alpha between the two parents and cannot cleanly answer the stated independence question — a correlation check or a residualized second leg would be far more informative than a blended composite.

This is an explicitly acknowledged cosmetic re-parameterization of the archive winner `profitable_capex_own_history_low` (same profitability gate, same own-history capex-intensity leg, only TS_RANK swapped for a current/MA5 ratio), so it tests measurement resolution rather than any new economic content and will be near-collinear with the existing signal.

Fully firm-demeaning both legs is a coherent and internally consistent response to the diagnosed style-absorption problem, though it overlaps materially with the gen-0 `margin_up_capex_down_trend` (profit rising while capex falls) and differs mainly in using own-mean deviations and a product instead of trends and a difference, so incremental information is uncertain.

Net debt issuance scaled by cash flow is a direct restatement of the well-documented net-debt-issuance/external-financing anomaly and largely duplicates the archive's `outside_capital_per_internal_dollar` (which already put DELTA(dltt) over max(oancf,dp) with a profitability gate and produced t=0.43 alpha), so it is a rediscovery on two fronts.

Acquirer underperformance and the acquisition component of asset growth are established published anomalies, and because aqc is zero for most firm-years the RANK leg collapses to a near-binary acquirer indicator with a massive tie block, making the "conditional" interaction effectively a profitability sort within non-acquirers.

Pairing an SG&A-intensity change with own-norm capex restraint is a genuinely new construct that avoids the RMW-loading level gate, but the sign is not obviously safe — a falling SG&A/sales ratio is mechanically produced by sales growth and is elsewhere read as underinvestment in intangibles — so the expected positive sign rests on a contestable premise.

Normalizing capex intensity by its own five-year maximum is a near-monotone transform of the archive winner's TS_RANK leg and is also highly redundant with proposal 1 in this same batch, so it cannot cleanly discriminate among own-history benchmarks and adds little beyond a third parameterization of an already-tested mechanism.

A single-operator extension of the archive's best signal, but the industry-demeaning of the own-norm capex deviation is economically motivated (idiosyncratic restraint vs. sector capex cycle) and directly targets the diagnosed FMB-strong/alpha-weak pattern, so it is a defensible if incremental test rather than a cosmetic rescaling.

The inventory-intensity leg edges toward the well-documented inventory-growth anomaly (Thomas–Zhang, Belo–Lin), but recasting it as an own-norm deviation interacted with a profit windfall is a legitimate and clearly stated test of whether the mechanism is capex-specific or general operating-asset restraint.

The two legs are mechanically linked — above-norm EBITDA largely produces above-norm cash balances — so the product is closer to a squared profitability-windfall signal than to a measure of a deliberate retention-versus-reinvestment policy, and the cash-holdings level effect (Palazzo 2012) is itself a known anomaly.

The hypothesis claims a screen ("requiring that revenue still be expanding") and the type is declared conditional, but SUMRANK implements a purely additive tilt in which a large profitability deviation can fully offset outright revenue contraction, so the expression does not do what the economics asks and also imports an uncontrolled sales-growth tilt.

A well-motivated repair of the archive's worst failure that replaces scale-driven headcount growth with own-norm labor intensity, though it partially overlaps with the profitability leg (falling employees per sales dollar mechanically accompanies margin expansion) and will read in part as a labor-productivity signal.

Both legs are driven by the same underlying fact of a stagnant capital base — a firm that stops investing automatically shows above-norm sales-to-gross-PPE and below-norm capex-to-net-PPE — so the "joint occurrence" claim is undermined by mechanical denominator overlap and the signal risks being a doubled low-investment bet rather than utilization × restraint.

This is a pure recombination of three already-evaluated archive legs (gross-margin windfall, industry-demeaned own-norm capex restraint, sales-growth MIN screen) with no new economic content, and stacking the three best-performing components in a strict triple conjunction mostly selects on prior in-sample noise while shrinking the effective long portfolio.

A legitimate but modest horizon variant of the archive winner `own_norm_profit_up_capex_down` — the 3y-vs-5y MA crossover genuinely separates regime shifts from project lumpiness, though the two windows overlap heavily so the test has less discriminating power than claimed and the profitability leg is left unchanged.

Well-constructed and internally consistent — both legs are same-unit asset-scaled own-norm deviations so the subtraction is economically meaningful (essentially the own-norm deviation in EBITDA-minus-capex per asset), and testing magnitude against the family's ubiquitous rank-product form answers a structural question the archive cannot; the main risk is that un-ranked raw deviations leave the FMB slope outlier-sensitive despite winsorization.

The "profit windfall" leg is not a profitability measure at all — (oancf − ib)/at is negative total accruals, so the signal rewards firms whose *earnings fall relative to cash flow*, which both contradicts the stated hypothesis of a cash-backed profit improvement and largely rediscovers the Sloan accruals anomaly in change form.

A coherent moderation hypothesis that is deliberately informative against `asset_light_margin_rents`, but multiplying by a strictly positive rank imposes a standalone monotone tilt toward capital-intensive firms rather than a clean interaction test, so a positive or negative result will be hard to attribute to moderation versus the level effect of asset heaviness.

A defensible dynamic recasting of the archive's high-slope R&D-mix signal, but the ratio's denominator means a rising xrd/(capx+xrd) deviation can be driven purely by falling capex — partially re-encoding the restraint leg rather than isolating a reallocation-toward-innovation decision — and xrd coverage near 0.07 will limit portfolio reliability.

Because the own-norm deviation of (capx−dp)/ppent equals the deviation of capx/ppent minus the deviation of dp/ppent, and dp/ppent is highly persistent so its deviation is near zero, this leg is mechanically almost identical to the archived winner's restraint leg — a cosmetic variant rather than the claimed isolation of "expansion" capex.

The claimholder moderator is a genuinely new dimension for this family and the sign logic is internally consistent, but the third rank leg embeds the well-documented low-net-debt/high-cash-holdings premium as a standalone effect, so any alpha gain will need to be shown not to come from that leg alone (and triple rank multiplication risks a concentrated, unstable long side).

This is essentially the already-tested additive netting (unreinvested_windfall_in_asset_units, fmb 1.88 / talpha 2.35) with z-scoring and a different capex scaler, and the z-scoring destroys the very unit-commensurability that made the asset-unit netting economically interpretable — a re-run rather than a substantively different construction (also mislabeled interaction_type "ratio" for a difference).

Symmetrically industry-demeaning both legs is a single-operator extension of an archived variant, but it tests a well-posed economic question — whether the sector-cyclical component of profitability improvement is signal or noise relative to FF5 — and the expected sign follows correctly from the expression.

A clean complementary diagnostic to the gen-5 smoothed-restraint result that isolates which leg must be fresh versus durable, though the MA3-minus-MA5 windfall uses overlapping windows and will be a weak, slow-moving trend measure, so a muted cross-sectional slope is a real risk.

Averaging two ranked readings of the same latent earning-power improvement is a legitimate measurement-error reduction rather than screen-stacking, and the diagnosis (equal alphas, very different Sharpes) supports it — but since both constituents are already archived, the expected information gain is incremental and the result may simply land between them.

A legitimate complementarity test of two separately-validated archive legs, but it is combinatorial rather than new economics, and it stacks a third rank onto a moderator (net debt/assets) that already collapsed the cross-sectional slope to 1.52 in `harvest_that_accrues_to_equity` — likely a non-monotone, low-leverage/cash-holdings style tilt that industry-demeaning the other two legs cannot repair.

This is a single-operator ablation of an existing archive signal (adding IND_ADJ to the net-debt leg only) rather than a substantively different construction; the attribution question it poses is worth answering, but the answer is largely predictable — capital structure is heavily industry-determined, so demeaning will mostly strip the sector tilt and leave a weaker, mechanically similar version of a signal whose FMB slope was already insignificant.

The moderator RATIO(xint, ebitda) is sign-unstable — for negative or near-zero EBITDA the ratio flips negative and NEG() then assigns the *highest* rank to exactly the distressed firms the hypothesis wants to exclude, so the expression's natural direction contradicts the stated mechanism; interest coverage is also a well-worn distress/leverage proxy rather than a novel claimholder measure.

Wrapping one IND_ADJ around the capex leg of `capex_shortfall_given_a_windfall` is a cosmetic variant, not a new mechanism, and it introduces a subtle inconsistency the reasoning misses: after industry demeaning, the zero assigned to non-windfall firms is no longer the centre of the conditional distribution, so masked firms will systematically drift into one tail in industries with above- or below-average capex deviations.

NEG((Δceq − ib)/at) is the clean-surplus net payout / net equity issuance measure — a direct rediscovery of the well-documented net-issuance and net-payout-yield anomalies (Daniel–Titman, Pontiff–Woodgate, Boudoukh et al.) — and the reasoning's claim that it is "not a financing-anomaly proxy" is exactly backwards; it will also be contaminated by write-offs, dividends-in-kind and other clean-surplus violations.

A coherent, parsimonious two-leg combination of two independently validated modifications (durability on the profitability leg, peer-demeaning on both), with a well-posed question about whether sector purity survives when the windfall is measured as a persistent rather than transitory improvement — though it remains an incremental recombination rather than a new mechanism, and IND_ADJ of an already own-norm-demeaned quantity risks double-differencing away most of the surviving variation.

This is a strictly monotone (outer RANK) re-encoding of the archived `peer_relative_harvest_with_slack`, so it re-proposes an already-evaluated signal with identical firm ordering and, as the author concedes, identical portfolio statistics — a diagnostic on FMB regressor distribution, not a new economic signal.

Averaging the slack and asset-vintage moderators is a genuinely different construction from either archived triple product, though the archive is internally contradictory about the sign of ppent/ppegt (`profitable_old_capital_base` treats low net-to-gross as the good state, `harvest_with_young_capital_runway` the opposite) and the vintage leg carried essentially no cross-sectional slope (fmb 0.14), so noise reduction is speculative.

A weakest-link gate is not a monotone transform of the product and so constitutes a substantively different aggregation of the same three legs, giving a clean test of whether the alpha lives in the extreme corner or in joint moderate satisfaction — though it remains a functional-form experiment on well-trodden legs rather than new economics.

Pairing the archive's best-slope profitability leg with its best-alpha moderator is the obvious and defensible next step and is not a rediscovery, but it is an incremental recombination of two evaluated signals, and the claimed benefit of the inert outer RANK applies only to the FMB regression, not to the alpha.

Decomposing net-debt-to-assets into a cash-coverage moderator is a real attribution test that can distinguish a distributable-cash mechanism from a low-leverage style tilt, and the depreciation floor sensibly handles debt-free firms, though cash-holdings premia are themselves a documented anomaly that could partly account for any gain.

The expression multiplies a leg whose standalone expected sign is positive (peer-relative profitability improvement) by an investment leg expected negative and then asserts an unambiguously negative composite sign, so the predicted direction is not implied by the construction; moreover profitable-high-investment underperformance is essentially the published q-theory investment anomaly conditioned on profitability.

This is the archived min_gate_peer_harvest_slack with the net-debt moderator swapped for a mechanically near-identical cash-to-debt measure (net debt already nets out cash), and the stated justification is factually wrong — the net-debt product form delivered the largest alpha (7.0%, peer_relative_harvest_with_slack), not the 6.1% cash-coverage version — so the proposal is a cosmetic variant built on a misread of the archive.

A single, economically motivated leg substitution (3y-vs-5y durable rents for the 1y windfall) inside the archived gate, testing whether the durability leg's strong slopes survive the aggregation that produced the strong alphas — incremental but a legitimate and interpretable one-factor-at-a-time test.

Adding the peer-relative revenue-growth screen as a fourth floor condition is a genuine extension rather than a restatement, and the pre-registered interpretation of a degradation (moderators are substitutes / over-restriction) makes the test informative either way, though the long leg risks becoming a narrow, unstable intersection.

The asymmetric structure — rank the harvest interaction first, then cap it by slack — poses a real aggregation question that neither the symmetric three-way gate nor the triple product answers, and the expression correctly implements the stated hypothesis on a common rank scale.

Substituting a level (structurally low reinvestment rate) for a deviation (below own norm) is an economically meaningful distinction between a standing policy and a mispriced surprise, and comparing gate versus the archived product form of the same legs cleanly attributes the difference, though the leg is close to the well-known asset-growth/investment anomaly in industry-adjusted dress.

A strict two-leg ablation of an already-archived three-leg gate is low in novelty, but it is the missing attribution baseline separating aggregation effects from the claimholder moderator and is the most parsimonious candidate for a final reported signal, so it is worth the cheap test.

validation_diagnostics.message: proposal expression does not use any variable exclusive to required theme: investment (variables shared across the paired themes, e.g. common denominators like 'at', do not count as evidence for either theme)
